guidetextdraw_copy._value:
Understanding Your Catalog Year 

As a student, the requirements that are in place when you are admitted to the university are the same requirements that you will follow until graduation. Students in the state of California also have the right to follow the requirements based on when they first began continuous attendance at another CSU or community college, or the rights during the term they are to graduate. The wording of the regulation is below under “Continuous Attendance and Catalog Rights.” 

Catalog Year Change Form 

The Catalog Year form is for updating your existing catalog year in order to change the requirements you must complete for graduation. Please read these about filling out the form carefully. 

  • If you want to change your catalog year to your CSUF admit term, the term you began continuous attendance at a Community College or another CSU, or your graduation term, please fill out the Standard Catalog Year Change Form

Continuous Attendance and Catalog Rights 

Students who have been enrolled either at a California Community College or a CSU campus for at least one semester or two-quarters of consecutive calendar years are considered to be “in continuous attendance.” 

Continuous attendance affects the requirements you must meet to graduate from a CSU campus. Institutions occasionally modify graduation requirements. If you have been in continuous attendance, you may choose to meet the CSU campus graduation requirements in the CSU catalog that was in effect in any of the three instances: 

  1. At the time you began continuous attendance at the California Community College, 
  2. At the time you transferred to the CSU campus, or 
  3. At the time you graduate from the CSU campus. 

By maintaining continuous attendance and selecting option (1) or (2), you can be assured that your CSU campus graduation requirements will not change. Your right to choose one of these options is called “catalog rights.” 

If you do not remain in continuous attendance, you will reestablish catalog rights at the time you reenroll in any California Community College or begin attending a CSU campus.
